question: What happens if a bicyclist disobeys traffic laws?
options: a: They can be issued a ticket.,b: They are exempt because traffic laws don’t apply to bicyclists.,c: They will only get a warning from law enforcement.
note: Bicyclists generally must follow the same traffic laws as drivers, including obeying signals, signs, and right-of-way rules. If a bicyclist breaks these laws, they can receive a traffic ticket just like a motor vehicle driver.

question: What is a speed limit?
options: a: The suggested speed under ideal conditions.,b: The legal maximum or minimum speed under ideal conditions.,c: The legal maximum or minimum speed under dangerous conditions.
note: A speed limit is the maximum (and sometimes minimum) legal speed allowed on a road under ideal conditions. You must still slow down below the posted limit when conditions are less than ideal, such as in bad weather, heavy traffic, school zones, or work zones.

question: Who has the right-of-way at a four-way stop if two drivers arrive simultaneously?
options: a: The driver on the left.,b: The driver on the right.,c: Neither driver needs to stop.
note: At a four-way stop, all drivers must come to a complete stop. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right has the right-of-way and should proceed first. The driver on the left must yield. If arrival times are different, the vehicle that stopped first goes first, regardless of side.

question: What does a regulatory sign with a red circle and slash indicate?
options: a: Drivers must stop completely.,b: An action is prohibited.,c: Some drivers must yield.
note: A red circle with a diagonal slash over a symbol means that the action shown is not allowed. For example, a right-turn arrow with a red circle and slash means no right turn at that location.

question: At what age must a child ride in the back seat of a vehicle?
options: a: Under 13.,b: Under 14.,c: Under 16.
note: In Washington State, children under 13 years old must ride in the back seat when practical because it is safer in a crash, especially with airbags in the front. The law is under 13, not under 14, 15, or 16. Keeping younger passengers in the rear seat greatly reduces the risk of serious injury.

question: When may you cross a dashed white line?
options: a: At any time.,b: Only during daylight hours.,c: When safe to change lanes.
note: Dashed white lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross a dashed white line to change lanes or pass when it is safe and legal to do so, after checking mirrors and blind spots and signaling your intention.

question: What happens if a green arrow changes to a solid green light?
options: a: You may still turn but must yield to oncoming traffic.,b: You must proceed straight and cannot turn.,c: You retain the right-of-way to turn.
note: A green arrow gives you a protected turn with the right-of-way. When it changes to a solid green light, you may still turn in that direction, but it is no longer protected. You must yield to oncoming traffic, cyclists, and pedestrians before turning.

question: What must a driver do when dealing with pedestrians?
options: a: Make sure pedestrians see your vehicle.,b: Always yield and do whatever is necessary to avoid hitting pedestrians, even if they are not following the rules.,c: Yield only when pedestrians have the right-of-way.
note: Drivers must use extreme care around pedestrians. You must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and always do whatever is necessary to avoid hitting a pedestrian, even if the pedestrian is crossing incorrectly or does not have the right-of-way.

question: What must you do when meeting an oncoming vehicle on a narrow road?
options: a: Pull completely off the road.,b: Allow the oncoming vehicle half the road.,c: Demand they pull over.
note: On a narrow road, you must share the roadway so that each vehicle has enough space to pass safely. Slow down if needed and keep as far to the right as is safe, allowing the oncoming vehicle at least half of the main-traveled portion of the road. Never force the other driver off the road or insist they yield all the space.

question: What does an arrow painted on the pavement mean?
options: a: Drivers in that lane must stop before following the arrow.,b: Drivers in that lane may follow the arrow if they choose.,c: Drivers in that lane must follow the arrow’s direction.
note: Arrows painted on the pavement show which direction traffic in that lane must go, such as straight, left turn, or right turn. When you are in a lane with a directional arrow, you are required to follow that direction unless a traffic sign or signal clearly allows something different.

question: What does a red and white triangular sign at an intersection indicate?
options: a: Always stop completely.,b: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.,c: Slow down and yield to traffic or pedestrians.
note: A red and white triangular sign is a yield sign. You must slow down, be ready to stop, and yield the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians already in or approaching the intersection. Stop if needed to avoid interfering with other road users.

question: What do speed limit signs indicate?
options: a: Suggested speeds for the area.,b: Maximum or minimum legal speed.,c: Speed for heavy traffic.
note: Speed limit signs show the maximum or sometimes minimum legal speed under ideal conditions. You must slow down below the posted limit when road, traffic, or weather conditions make the posted speed unsafe.

question: Where should your car be positioned to make a right turn?
options: a: Near the center of the street.,b: Close to the left side.,c: Close to the right side.
note: To make a right turn safely, you should position your vehicle as close as practicable to the right-hand curb or edge of the roadway. This helps prevent you from swinging wide into another lane and keeps you predictable to other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians.

question: What color are guide signs that provide directional and mileage information?
options: a: Red.,b: Green.,c: Yellow.
note: Guide or destination signs that show directions and distances are green with white lettering. They help you find routes, exits, and destinations, especially in unfamiliar areas.

question: What does a traffic light with a green arrow and red light mean?
options: a: Wait for a solid green light to proceed.,b: Drive only in the direction of the green arrow.,c: Drive straight ahead only.
note: A green arrow means you have a protected turn in the direction of the arrow, even if the main light is red. You may proceed only in the direction of the arrow and must still yield to pedestrians and any traffic already in the intersection.

question: At an intersection with a yield sign, you should:
options: a: Yield only to traffic on the left.,b: Always stop before entering.,c: Slow down and yield to traffic in the intersection.
note: A yield sign means you must slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary, yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection or on the road you are entering. You do not have to stop if the way is clear.

question: When may you cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a: To pass a slow-moving truck.,b: To turn into a driveway.,c: To pass another car.
note: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing in either direction. You may cross them only to make a left turn into or from a driveway, side road, or alley, to enter or exit a highway, or to make a permitted U‑turn. You may not cross them just to pass slower traffic.

question: What should you do at an intersection with a green light but pedestrians crossing against the red?
options: a: Honk your horn.,b: Speed up to pass pedestrians.,c: Stop to let pedestrians cross.
note: Stop and yield to pedestrians crossing, even if they’re in the wrong, to ensure their safety.

question: What is the correct order of traffic lights from top to bottom?
options: a: Green,b: Red,c: Yellow
note: On vertically mounted traffic signals, the red light is always at the top, yellow in the middle, and green at the bottom. This standard order helps drivers quickly recognize the signal even from a distance or in poor visibility.

question: Where are stop lines located?
options: a: At intersections and crosswalks.,b: Next to churches and schools.,c: In curves and on hills.
note: Stop lines are solid white lines painted on the road at intersections and crosswalks. They show you where you must stop your vehicle so that you stay clear of cross traffic, pedestrians, and the crosswalk area.

question: What do downward-facing triangular signs indicate?
options: a: Construction zones.,b: School zones.,c: Yield to traffic or pedestrians.
note: A downward-facing triangle is the standard shape for a yield sign. It tells you to slow down, be ready to stop, and yield the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians already in or close to the intersection. Proceed only when it is safe.

question: What do double solid yellow lines in the middle of a road mean?
options: a: Pedestrian crossing ahead.,b: Passing is not permitted from either direction except for left turns into or out of a driveway or side road.,c: Railroad crossing ahead.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean vehicles in both directions may not cross the lines to pass. The main exception is when you are turning left into or out of a driveway, side road, or alley. You must never use the opposing lane to pass another vehicle across double solid yellow lines.

question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass?
options: a:Yes,b:No.,c:You yes
note: Double solid yellow centerlines mean traffic in both directions is prohibited from crossing to pass. You may only cross them when making a left turn into or out of a driveway, side road, or business entrance, or when directed by law enforcement or traffic control devices.

question: When must you stop for a school bus?
options: a: If parked with no one in it.,b: When approaching without flashing lights.,c: On a two-lane highway with red lights flashing.
note: On a two‑lane road, traffic in both directions must stop when a school bus has its red lights flashing and the stop arm extended. Remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn, watching for children who may be crossing the road.

question: When may you cross solid yellow lines?
options: a: To pass same-direction traffic.,b: During daylight hours only.,c: When making a turn.
note: A single solid yellow line generally marks the center of a two‑way road and warns that passing is discouraged or prohibited. You should not cross it to pass other vehicles. You may cross a solid yellow line only when making a left turn into or from a driveway, side road, or alley, or for a legal U‑turn where allowed and safe.

question: How should bicyclists ride on sidewalks or in crosswalks?
options: a: Take the right-of-way.,b: Yield to pedestrians.,c: Ride without signaling before passing.
note: When riding on sidewalks or in crosswalks where it is allowed, bicyclists must ride slowly and always yield to pedestrians. Treat pedestrians as having the right-of-way and give them plenty of space.

question: When are you required to stop your vehicle?
options: a: At a red light.,b: When a traffic officer signals you to stop.,c: At an intersection with a stop sign.,d: All of the above.
note: You are required to stop at a steady or flashing red light, at stop signs, and whenever a traffic officer directs you to stop. Failing to stop in any of these situations is illegal and dangerous because cross‑traffic or pedestrians may be entering the intersection.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
options: a: Merging traffic.,b: Proceed with caution.,c: Pedestrian crossing.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution. You do not have to stop, but you must be alert for other vehicles, pedestrians, or hazards.

question: Who has the right-of-way in a crosswalk marked by two solid white lines?
options: a: Motor vehicles.,b: Pedestrians in the crosswalk.,c: No one.
note: When pedestrians are in a marked crosswalk, they have the right-of-way. Drivers must yield and, if necessary, stop to allow pedestrians to cross safely before proceeding.

question: A red flashing traffic light is equivalent to:
options: a: A yield sign.,b: A stop sign.,c: A solid red light.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to go.

question: What are the colors of warning signs for upcoming hazards?
options: a: Black on white.,b: Black on yellow.,c: White on blue.
note: Most general warning signs that alert you to upcoming hazards are yellow with black symbols or lettering. These signs warn about curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, and other conditions ahead. Work zone warning signs are usually orange with black symbols or lettering.

question: What are signs that require drivers to obey an instruction called?
options: a: Information signs.,b: Regulatory signs.,c: Warning signs.
note: Regulatory signs tell you what you must do or must not do, such as speed limits, stop signs, and no‑turn signs. Because they state legal requirements, failing to obey them can result in traffic tickets or other penalties.

question: You are on a two-way street, stopped at an intersection. Can you legally turn left on a red light into a one-way street?
options: a: Only if a left turn sign is posted.,b: Yes, if traffic allows unless prohibited.,c: No, You must wait for the green light.,d: Only if there is a green arrow with the red light.
note: In many states, you may turn left on a red light from a one-way street onto another one-way street, after stopping and yielding, unless a sign prohibits it. However, turning left on red from a two-way street onto a one-way street is not universally allowed and is illegal in several states. Because this rule is not uniform across the U.S., you must follow the specific law in your state as described in your state driver handbook.

question: What should you do at an uncontrolled intersection?
options: a: Maintain speed and proceed without checking for other traffic.,b: Slow, be prepared to stop, check all directions, and proceed only when safe.,c: Yield to any vehicles already in the intersection and to vehicles on your right if you arrive at the same time.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, you must slow down, be ready to stop, and look carefully in all directions before proceeding. You must yield to any vehicle already in the intersection and to vehicles approaching from the right if you arrive at the same time. Coming to a full stop is often the safest choice when visibility is limited or traffic is close.

question: What should you do to turn right at a steady red light?
options: a: Slow down and look for traffic before turning.,b: Stop, signal, and turn when safe if not prohibited.,c: Signal and wait for a green light.
note: At a steady red light, you must come to a complete stop before the crosswalk or limit line. If right turns on red are allowed at that intersection, signal, yield to pedestrians and other traffic, and then turn right when it is safe.

question: What does a steady green light at an intersection mean?
options: a: Stop and check for traffic before proceeding.,b: Slow down and prepare to stop.,c: Drive through if the road is clear.
note: A steady green light means you may go straight or turn, if not prohibited, but only if the intersection is clear. You must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to oncoming traffic when turning left. Green never means you can proceed without checking for other road users.

question: Where should you stop at an intersection with a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk?
options: a: No stop is required.,b: Slow down to check traffic.,c: Stop where you can see approaching traffic.
note: At a stop sign with no stop line or crosswalk, you must stop before entering the intersection at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you have a clear view of approaching traffic, without moving into the intersection.

question: When can you proceed through an intersection with a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk?
options: a: After slowing to check traffic, without fully stopping.,b: After coming to a complete stop where you can see traffic and verifying it’s safe.,c: After stopping exactly 20 feet before the intersection.
note: At a stop sign with no stop line or crosswalk, you must come to a complete stop before entering the intersection, at the point where you can best see approaching traffic. After stopping and checking in all directions, proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe to enter the intersection.

question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?
options: a: If a stop sign is posted.,b: If a crossing gate is lowered.,c: If crossing lights are flashing.,d: All of the above.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing any time a stop sign is posted, the crossing gate is lowered or starting to lower, the red warning lights are flashing, a flagger signals you to stop, or you can see or hear a train that is close enough to be a danger. Never drive around lowered gates or ignore flashing lights, even if you do not see a train.

question: What shape is a stop sign?
options: a: Circle.,b: Square.,c: Octagon.
note: A stop sign is an octagon. This unique eight-sided shape helps drivers recognize it quickly from a distance and even from the back, reminding them that all approaching traffic must come to a complete stop before proceeding when safe.

question: What is the height requirement for children under eight to use a safety restraint system under Washington's Child Restraint Law?
options: a: 4 feet 9 inches.,b: 5 feet.,c: 5 feet 5 inches.
note: Under Washington's Child Restraint Law, children under age eight who are shorter than 4 feet 9 inches must be secured in an appropriate child safety restraint system rather than just a seat belt. Once a child is at least 4 feet 9 inches tall, they may use a properly fitted seat belt. Height, not 4 feet 11 inches, is the key threshold.

question: When a school bus is stopped off the road without flashing lights, you should:
options: a: Stop regardless of your direction.,b: Stop only if on the same side as the bus.,c: Pass with caution.
note: The special stop requirement applies when a school bus is displaying flashing red lights or an extended stop arm. If a bus is stopped off the road without flashing lights or a stop arm, you are not required to stop, but you must pass slowly and carefully, watching for children who may enter the roadway unexpectedly.

question: When may you continue through a yellow light?
options: a: If an emergency vehicle is crossing.,b: If pedestrians are crossing.,c: If already in the intersection.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You must stop if you can do so safely before the intersection. If the light turns yellow after you have already entered the intersection, continue through carefully; stopping in the intersection is unsafe.

question: What should you do at a steady red traffic light?
options: a: Drive through if no traffic.,b: Proceed with right-of-way after stopping and yielding where a turn on red is allowed.,c: Stop completely and remain stopped until the light changes or a legal turn on red is allowed.
note: A steady red light means you must come to a complete stop before the crosswalk or stop line and remain stopped until the light turns green, unless you are making a permitted turn on red after stopping and yielding. You may not drive straight through a red light.

question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?
options: a: Increase speed.,b: Stop completely.,c: Proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard or a need for extra caution. You do not have to stop, but you should slow down, look carefully for cross traffic, pedestrians, or other dangers, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: What does a stop sign mean?
options: a: Slow down and stop if cars approach.,b: Come to a full stop and proceed when safe.,c: Proceed carefully without always stopping.
note: A stop sign means you must come to a complete stop at the limit line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection. After stopping, yield to pedestrians and other vehicles, then proceed only when it is safe.

question: What does a green arrow with a red light at an intersection mean?
options: a: Stop even if turning in the arrow’s direction.,b: Proceed straight through the intersection.,c: Turn safely in the direction of the arrow.
note: A green arrow with a red light means you may turn only in the direction of the arrow, and other movements are stopped by the red light. You must still yield to pedestrians and any traffic already in the intersection before turning.

question: What does a No Standing sign indicate?
options: a: You can park if the driver stays in the vehicle.,b: Stopping is never permitted at this location.,c: You may briefly stop to pick up or drop off passengers.
note: A No Standing sign means you may stop only briefly to pick up or drop off passengers, but you may not wait for them or load/unload goods. Parking or standing for any other reason is not allowed in that area.

question: What does a yellow and black diamond-shaped sign indicate?
options: a: Directs you to nearby cities or towns.,b: Warns of road conditions or hazards.,c: Informs about traffic laws.
note: Yellow and black diamond‑shaped signs are warning signs. They alert you to upcoming road conditions or hazards such as curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, or changes in road surface so you can adjust your driving in advance.

question: When must drivers yield to a pedestrian?
options: a: Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road.,b: Only when the pedestrian is in a marked or unmarked crosswalk.,c: Drivers must use extreme care and be prepared to yield to pedestrians, even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly.
note: Drivers must use extreme care around pedestrians and do everything possible to avoid hitting them, even if the pedestrian is acting unsafely. You must always yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and should be prepared to yield anywhere people are crossing, because a vehicle can cause far more harm than a person on foot.

question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?
options: a: School zones.,b: Railroad crossings.,c: No passing zones.
note: A crossbuck sign marks a railroad crossing. It means you must look and listen for trains, slow down, and be prepared to stop. You must yield the right‑of‑way to any approaching train and never try to beat a train through the crossing.

question: Where can bicyclists legally ride?
options: a: In a left turn only lane without turning.,b: On freeways where signs prohibit it.,c: On the roadway, shoulder, or bicycle lane.
note: Bicyclists are generally allowed to ride on the roadway, on the shoulder, or in a designated bicycle lane, and they must follow the same basic rules of the road as motor vehicles. Whether bicycles may legally use sidewalks depends on local laws, so sidewalk riding is not always permitted everywhere.

question: What must you do at an intersection with a flashing red light?
options: a: Slow down and drive carefully.,b: Turn right or left.,c: Stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when the intersection is clear.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, yield to pedestrians and any vehicles with the right-of-way, and then proceed only when it is safe and the intersection is clear. You do not have to wait for the light to change; you proceed after stopping and yielding.

question: When there are no signs or lane markings to control turning, how should you turn?
options: a: Stop before turning.,b: Turn from the lane closest to your direction.,c: Turn from the center lane.
note: When there are no signs or lane markings, you should turn from the lane that is closest to the direction you want to go and enter the nearest lane going your way. This reduces conflicts with other vehicles and keeps turns predictable and safe.

question: What must you do when making a right turn on a green light?
options: a: Maintain normal speed if the way is clear and you have yielded.,b: Stop and check for police.,c: Yield to pedestrians and any traffic already in or entering the intersection.
note: When turning right on a green light, you may proceed without stopping if the way is clear, but you must always yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any vehicles already in or entering the intersection. Green means you may go only when it is safe and you do not interfere with others who have the right‑of‑way.

question: On roads with more than two lanes traveling in the same direction. You should:
options: a: Speed up and not allow anyone to pass you when traveling in the right lane.,b: Use the middle lane for normal through traffic when available.,c: Use the left lane for passing only.
note: On multi-lane roads, the left lane is generally used for passing or faster-moving traffic, while the right lane is usually for slower traffic and entering or exiting. The middle lane (if present) is typically for through traffic at normal speeds, not specifically for slower speeds. Always keep right except to pass when safe and legal.

question: What is the default speed limit in cities and towns unless otherwise posted?
options: a: 15 mph.,b: 25 mph in many residential or business districts (varies by state).,c: There is no single nationwide default; obey posted signs and your state’s basic speed law.
note: Many states use 25 mph as a common default in residential or business districts, but there is no single nationwide default city/town speed limit. Some states use 30 mph or other values. Drivers must always follow the posted speed limit and know the specific default limits for the state in which they are driving.

question: What are the most effective safety restraints in a traffic crash?
options: a: Only a lap and shoulder belt.,b: Only an airbag.,c: Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
note: The safest protection in a crash comes from using both the lap/shoulder belt and the airbag together. Seat belts keep you properly positioned and prevent you from being thrown forward, while airbags provide extra cushioning in moderate to severe frontal crashes. Airbags are designed to work with seat belts, not replace them.

question: When must you yield to other drivers?
options: a: When entering from a garage or alley.,b: At an unmarked intersection with a vehicle on your left.,c: When your signal is a green arrow.
note: When entering a roadway from a driveway, alley, or garage, you must yield to all traffic already on the road and to pedestrians on any sidewalk you cross. Vehicles already on the main road have the right‑of‑way, and you must wait until it is safe before pulling out.

question: What does coming to a complete stop and yielding at an intersection correspond to?
options: a: A solid green light.,b: A flashing yellow light.,c: A flashing red light.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, then yield to any vehicles or pedestrians already in or close to the intersection. Proceed only when it is safe, just as you would at a stop sign.

question: What does a single broken yellow line in the center of a two-lane road mean?
options: a: Lanes move in the same direction.,b: Lanes move in opposite directions.,c: Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is never allowed.
note: A single broken yellow line in the center of a two-lane road separates traffic moving in opposite directions. You may cross this line to pass another vehicle when it is safe and when passing is not otherwise prohibited by signs or additional markings.

question: What purpose do highway markings serve?
options: a: Found only in construction zones.,b: Provide information to drivers.,c: Usually unimportant.
note: Highway markings provide important information about lane use, passing zones, where you must stop, and changes in the roadway. They help you position your vehicle correctly and drive safely.

question: What must a driver do when approaching a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a: Merge to the right.,b: Slow down without stopping.,c: Stop and proceed when safe.
note: A flashing red signal means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for cross traffic and pedestrians, yield to anyone with the right‑of‑way, and then proceed only when it is safe. At railroad crossings, flashing red lights mean a train is approaching and you must stop and not proceed until the lights stop and it is clearly safe.

question: What do pentagonal signs signify?
options: a: Speed limits.,b: No passing zones.,c: School zones.
note: Pentagon-shaped (five-sided) signs are used for school zones and school crossings. When you see a pentagonal sign, slow down, watch carefully for children, and be prepared to stop for pedestrians in or near the roadway.

question: What does a solid white line slanting to the left on the right edge of the highway show?
options: a: You must turn left soon.,b: An intersection is ahead.,c: The road narrows ahead.
note: A solid white line on the right edge of the highway that slants or angles toward the center of the road shows that the edge of the roadway is moving inward and the lane or road is narrowing. It helps you stay in your lane and prepare to adjust your position or speed as the roadway becomes narrower.

question: What do work zone signs indicate?
options: a: It is summer.,b: Stop and back up.,c: Less than ideal driving conditions.
note: Orange work zone signs warn that road work or construction is present. Lanes may be narrowed, workers and equipment may be close to traffic, and surfaces or patterns can change. You should slow down, increase following distance, and be prepared for sudden stops or lane shifts.

question: How can you use a shared center lane on a two-way roadway?
options: a: Use it to pass.,b: Drive in it during rush hour.,c: Use it only for left turns and travel in it only briefly before turning.
note: A shared center left‑turn lane is used only for making or preparing for a left turn from either direction, or for beginning a left turn into traffic after a side street or driveway. It is not for passing or for driving long distances. Many states limit how far you may travel in this lane (often about 200–300 feet), so you should enter it shortly before your turn and leave it as soon as it is safe.

question: When entering public traffic from a driveway or private road, a driver should:
options: a: Force their way into traffic.,b: Yield to vehicles on the public road.,c: Assume the right-of-way.
note: When you enter a public road from a driveway, alley, or private road, you must stop if necessary and yield to all vehicles and pedestrians already on the public road. They have the right‑of‑way, and you may only pull out when there is a safe gap in traffic.

question: What should you do if a traffic light changes to solid yellow at an intersection?
options: a: Treat as a caution sign.,b: Stop immediately.,c: Stop unless too close to stop safely.
note: A solid yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You must stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are so close to the intersection when the light turns yellow that stopping would be unsafe (for example, you would have to brake very hard or might be hit from behind), you should continue carefully through the intersection.

question: What is used on highways to direct drivers into proper lanes for turning?
options: a: Flashing red lights.,b: Flashing yellow lights.,c: Lane-use arrows and white lane markings.
note: On highways, lane-use control for turns is provided by white lane lines together with painted arrows and overhead or roadside signs. The key element that directs drivers into the proper lane for turning is the lane-use arrows painted on the pavement, not just the white edge line on the side of the road.

question: What does a solid white line in the center of a two-lane road indicate?
options: a: Lanes move in opposite directions.,b: Lanes move in the same direction.,c: Lanes move in opposite directions.
note: A solid white line is used to separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction and to mark the right edge of the roadway. When the line is solid, you should not change lanes or pass except to avoid a hazard, because it is intended to discourage or prohibit lane changes.

question: When turning left at an intersection, drivers should:
options: a: Wait in the intersection until the light turns yellow.,b: Wait for the green arrow before turning.,c: Move into the intersection on green, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, and turn left only when it is safe.
note: When turning left on a solid green light, you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. You may carefully move into the intersection and wait with your wheels straight until there is a safe gap to turn. A green arrow gives you a protected turn, but you are not required to wait for a green arrow if you have a solid green and a safe opening.

question: What does a flashing yellow arrow at a traffic signal mean?
options: a: Merge in the arrow’s direction.,b: Stop completely.,c: Turn left after yielding to traffic and pedestrians.
note: A flashing yellow arrow for a left turn means you may turn left, but only after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. The turn is not protected, so oncoming traffic has the right-of-way.

question: What does a steady yellow arrow at a traffic signal mean?
options: a: Merge in the arrow’s direction.,b: Slow down and stop if you can do so safely; complete the turn if you are already in or too close to the intersection.,c: Turn left without stopping as long as you yield.
note: A steady yellow arrow means the protected turn phase is ending and a red arrow is about to appear. You should slow down and stop if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection or too close to stop safely, complete the turn with caution before the light turns red.

question: What does a double solid yellow line in the center of a two-lane road mean?
options: a: Lanes move in the same direction.,b: Lanes move in opposite directions.,c: Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
note: A double solid yellow line in the center of a two‑lane road means traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed from either direction. You may not cross these lines to pass another vehicle, but you may cross them carefully to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe.

question: What color are pavement markings separating traffic lanes moving in opposite directions?
options: a: Yellow.,b: White.,c: Yellow and white.
note: Yellow pavement markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads. White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction and also mark the right edge of the roadway.

question: What lighting is required for a bicycle at night?
options: a: White headlight visible for 300 feet.,b: White headlight visible for 400 feet.,c: White headlight visible for 500 feet.
note: A bicycle at night must have a white headlight visible for 500 feet and a red reflector visible for 600 feet.

question: When must you stop for a school bus on a two-lane, two-way roadway?
options: a: If red warning lights are flashing.,b: If yellow lights are flashing off-road.,c: Only if children are crossing.
note: On a two-lane, two-way roadway, you must stop for a school bus when its red lights are flashing and the stop arm is extended, no matter which direction you are traveling. You remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. The presence of children crossing is assumed when the red lights are on, so you must stop even if you do not immediately see children.

question: How should a seat belt be adjusted?
options: a: Hidden beneath the seat.,b: Buckled snugly across your hip bones and low on your abdomen, with the shoulder belt across the center of your chest.,c: Loose.
note: The lap portion of the seat belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and low on your abdomen, never across your stomach. The shoulder belt should cross the center of your chest and rest on your shoulder, not under your arm or behind your back, with only a small amount of slack so it can hold you firmly in a crash.

question: If two vehicles reach a four-way stop simultaneously, what should happen?
options: a: The vehicle on the right yields to the left.,b: Drivers use hand motions to communicate.,c: The vehicle on the left yields to the right.
note: At a four-way stop, when two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This right‑of‑way rule helps prevent confusion and collisions at intersections.

question: What should you do if you want to turn left at a green light with heavy oncoming traffic?
options: a: Use the next intersection.,b: Wait at the crosswalk.,c: Wait in the center of the intersection.
note: With a green light and no protected left arrow, you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. In many states you should pull into the intersection, keeping your wheels straight, and wait in the center until there is a safe gap to turn left or the light changes and oncoming traffic stops.

question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line signify?
options: a: Passing is allowed from the lane adjacent to the broken line.,b: Passing is permitted from either direction.,c: Passing is allowed from the lane next to the solid line.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only for traffic in the lane next to the broken line. Drivers in the lane next to the solid line must not cross it to pass. This marking is used on two‑way roads to control which direction may legally pass.

question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a: Never used as a traffic signal.,b: Same as a circular red light.,c: Drivers may turn in the arrow’s direction.
note: A solid red arrow means you must stop and remain stopped. It functions like a circular red light for that specific direction, and you may not proceed or turn in the direction of the arrow until it changes or a sign specifically allows a turn on red.

question: Who must wear a seat belt in a moving vehicle by law?
options: a: All occupants.,b: Only the driver.,c: Only under 18.
note: Seat belt laws vary by state. In Washington State, all occupants must wear seat belts, but in many other states only the driver and certain passengers (often front-seat and/or under a specific age) are legally required. Always follow your state’s specific seat belt law, and remember that wearing a seat belt is the safest choice for everyone in the vehicle.

question: From which lane should you start a left turn on multilane, one-way streets or highways?
options: a: The middle of the intersection.,b: The right lane.,c: The left lane.
note: On multilane, one‑way streets or highways, you should start a left turn from the leftmost lane because it lines you up correctly with the lane you will enter and reduces conflicts with other traffic.

question: Which lane should you be in to turn right?
options: a: The left lane.,b: The center lane.,c: The lane closest to the right.
note: To make a right turn, you should normally turn from the lane closest to the right curb or edge of the road. This keeps traffic organized and prevents conflicts with vehicles going straight or turning from other lanes.

question: What does a steady red traffic light mean?
options: a: Slow down and yield to other traffic.,b: Stop and look for danger before crossing.,c: Stop and don’t proceed until the light turns green.
note: A steady red light means you must come to a complete stop before the crosswalk or limit line and remain stopped until the light turns green and it is safe to proceed. In many states you may turn right on red (and left from a one‑way to a one‑way) after stopping and yielding, unless a sign prohibits it, but you may not go straight through on red.

question: What is true regarding seat belts and child restraints?
options: a: Never place infants or small children in front of an active airbag.,b: Airbags are safe for infants if they are in a rear-facing seat.,c: Ensure all passengers use seat belts or proper child restraints.
note: All occupants should always use seat belts or proper child restraints. Infants and small children should ride in the back seat, properly secured in child safety seats, and never in front of an active airbag. Using the correct restraint for each passenger greatly reduces the risk of injury in a crash.

question: What must you do when turning or changing lanes?
options: a: Always signal, even with no traffic.,b: Signal only if traffic is visible.,c: Signal only at night.
note: You must always signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb, even if you do not see other traffic. Signaling lets others know what you plan to do so they can adjust and avoid collisions.

question: What does an orange-colored sign indicate?
options: a: No passing zone.,b: Railroad crossing.,c: Construction or maintenance zone.
note: Orange traffic signs are used for construction, maintenance, and work zones. They warn you to slow down, be alert for workers and equipment, and follow any posted instructions.

question: When must you stop for a school bus with flashing red lights?
options: a: Only if children are crossing.,b: If traveling in the opposite direction on a multi-lane undivided road.,c: If traveling in either direction on an undivided road; on a divided road, only traffic going the same direction as the bus must stop.
note: You must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights when traveling in either direction on an undivided road. On a divided highway or a road with a physical median, only the traffic traveling in the same direction as the bus must stop; oncoming traffic on the other side of the median may proceed with caution.

question: When entering a roundabout, you must yield to:
options: a: Only pedestrians in the roundabout.,b: All vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians already in or crossing at the roundabout.,c: Only bicyclists in the roundabout.
note: When approaching a roundabout, you must yield to all traffic already in the circle, including vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians in crosswalks at the entries and exits. Enter only when there is a safe gap. Once inside the roundabout, you generally have the right‑of‑way over entering traffic but must still watch for pedestrians and cyclists at the exits.

question: What should you do at an intersection with a flashing yellow light?
options: a: Stop and wait.,b: Make a U-turn.,c: Drive carefully through.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution. Slow down, be prepared to stop, and carefully scan for cross traffic and pedestrians before going through the intersection.

question: What does a steady yellow light at an intersection indicate?
options: a: Yield to other vehicles.,b: Slow down and prepare to stop.,c: Go through the intersection.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and prepare to stop before the intersection. If you are so close that stopping safely is not possible when the light turns yellow, you may proceed with caution to clear the intersection.

question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?
options: a: Stop and wait for a green light.,b: Speed up to clear the intersection.,c: Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means you do not have to stop, but you must slow down and proceed with extra caution. Be prepared to yield to pedestrians and cross traffic that may not have to stop.

question: A flashing red traffic signal is equivalent to:
options: a: A yield sign.,b: A stop sign.,c: A slow sign.
note: A flashing red light means you must stop completely, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, you must yield to any traffic or pedestrians with the right‑of‑way and proceed only when it is safe.

question: When entering interstate traffic from an entrance ramp, a driver should:
options: a: Force their way into traffic.,b: Yield to vehicles already on the interstate.,c: Claim the right-of-way.
note: When entering an interstate, you must use the entrance and acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic and then merge when there is a safe gap. Vehicles already on the interstate have the right‑of‑way, so you must yield to them and adjust your speed or wait until it is safe to merge.

question: What should you do when approaching a school bus with its stop arm extended?
options: a: Stop and wait until the arm is withdrawn.,b: Honk before passing on the left.,c: Proceed if most kids have exited.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. This protects children who may be crossing in front of or behind the bus.

question: Which vehicle must yield when two vehicles enter an intersection simultaneously from different highways?
options: a: Either one.,b: The vehicle on the left.,c: The vehicle on the right.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, or where multiple vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This right‑of‑way rule helps prevent confusion and collisions when there are no signs or signals.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal indicates that a ____ light will soon appear.
options: a: Steady red.,b: Flashing yellow.,c: Steady green.
note: A steady yellow signal is a warning that the light will soon turn steady red. It gives drivers time to slow down and stop safely before entering the intersection, rather than braking suddenly at the moment the light turns red.

question: When approaching a roundabout, you must:
options: a: Stop in the intersection to yield to traffic on the right.,b: Enter regardless of other vehicles or pedestrians.,c: Drive around the circle to the right.
note: When using a roundabout, you must always drive around the central island to the right, never to the left. You must yield to traffic already in the roundabout and to pedestrians and bicyclists in crosswalks before you enter.

question: What does it mean when a driver’s left arm and hand are extended upward?
options: a: Turn left.,b: Turn right.,c: Stop.
note: When a vehicle’s left arm is extended straight out, it means a left turn. When the left arm and hand are raised upward, it signals a right turn. When the arm is pointed downward, it signals slowing or stopping.

question: When in a travel lane on the roadway, can you stop?
options: a: To drop off passengers or for non‑emergency reasons.,b: To look up an address or for non‑emergency reasons.,c: Only when required by traffic, signals, emergencies, or if your vehicle is disabled.
note: You should not stop and block a travel lane just to drop off passengers or look up an address. If you miss a turn or exit, keep going until you can safely pull off the road. However, you may need to stop in a travel lane when traffic requires it, at traffic signals, for emergency vehicles, or if your vehicle is disabled and cannot be moved.

question: What should you do when entering a street from a driveway?
options: a: Drive slowly to let others move.,b: Honk to warn others.,c: Stop and yield to vehicles and pedestrians.
note: When leaving a driveway, alley, or parking lot, you must stop before the sidewalk or edge of the road and yield to pedestrians and all traffic on the street. Enter only when it is safe and you will not force others to slow or stop suddenly.

question: What does a posted speed limit indicate?
options: a: A recommended driving speed.,b: The exact speed to avoid a ticket.,c: The maximum legal speed under ideal conditions.
note: A posted speed limit is the maximum legal speed allowed on that road in ideal conditions, not a target or guaranteed safe speed in all situations. You must slow down below the limit when conditions are poor, such as in rain, fog, heavy traffic, or road work, so you can stop safely and maintain control.

question: What do round signs indicate?
options: a: School zones.,b: No passing zones.,c: Railroad crossings.
note: Round yellow signs are used to warn of an upcoming railroad crossing. When you see a round railroad warning sign, slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop if necessary.

question: How should small children be secured in a vehicle?
options: a: Held by a strong adult.,b: Standing on the floor in the back.,c: In special child seats.
note: Small children must ride in properly installed child safety seats or booster seats that are appropriate for their age, weight, and height. In a crash or sudden stop, an adult cannot hold a child securely; only a correctly used child restraint system can provide the protection needed.

question: What does a No Stopping sign mean unless directed by a police officer?
options: a: You can stop only to avoid other traffic.,b: You may stop to unload packages.,c: You can stop only to let passengers out.
note: A No Stopping sign means you may not stop your vehicle in that area for passengers or loading, except when required to obey a traffic signal, follow a police officer’s directions, or avoid a collision. You must keep moving otherwise.

question: What must drivers obey regarding traffic signs and pavement markings?
options: a: Always obey them.,b: Treat them as suggestions.,c: Follow only with other traffic present.
note: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings are legal controls, not suggestions. You must always obey them to maintain safe, predictable traffic flow and avoid collisions and violations.

question: Bicycle lanes are marked with:
options: a: Double yellow lines.,b: Solid white lines.,c: One solid white line, and one solid yellow line.,d: Dashed white lines.
note: Bicycle lanes are usually marked with solid white lines that separate the bike lane from the motor vehicle travel lane. The lane often includes a bicycle symbol painted on the pavement. Drivers may not drive or park in a bike lane except where allowed by law, such as briefly entering it to turn when it is safe and legal.

question: When can you pass if the road has a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line with the broken line next to your lane?
options: a: Only in an emergency.,b: If on an expressway.,c: If traffic is clear.
note: A solid yellow line means no passing from that side, while a broken yellow line means passing is allowed from that side when it is safe. If the broken line is next to your lane, you may pass only when you have enough clear distance ahead and no oncoming traffic.

question: What does a steady red traffic signal require?
options: a: Stop before entering the intersection.,b: Slow down and yield to other traffic.,c: Stop and remain stopped until the light turns green and it is safe to proceed.
note: A steady red traffic signal means you must come to a complete stop before entering the intersection or crosswalk and remain stopped until the light turns green and it is safe to proceed. You do not proceed on red unless a specific sign or signal (such as a permitted right turn on red where allowed) clearly allows it and the way is clear.

question: At an uncontrolled intersection, you must:
options: a: Wait for other drivers to signal you to proceed.,b: Take the right-of-way cautiously.,c: Slow down and yield to vehicles already in the intersection or those that arrived first.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, no traffic signs or signals assign right‑of‑way, so drivers must use general right‑of‑way rules. You must slow down and be prepared to stop, yielding to any vehicle already in the intersection and to vehicles that arrive before you. Never assume you can just take the right‑of‑way; you only proceed when it is clearly safe.

question: If you arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as a vehicle on your right, you should:
options: a: Drive through and make the other vehicle stop.,b: Speed up to clear the intersection.,c: Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection (no signs or signals), you must yield the right‑of‑way to a vehicle that arrives at the same time from your right. Slowing down and letting the vehicle on your right go first reduces confusion and helps prevent side‑impact collisions.

question: What should you do at a steady yellow traffic light?
options: a: Accelerate to avoid a red light.,b: Proceed with right-of-way without slowing.,c: Slow down and stop if you can do so safely; proceed with caution if you are too close to stop safely or already in the intersection.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and stop if you can do so safely before the intersection. If you are too close to stop safely or are already in the intersection, continue through with caution.

question: When do you have the right-of-way when turning left?
options: a: On a solid green light.,b: On a flashing yellow light.,c: On a green arrow pointing left.
note: A green left arrow is a protected turn signal. Oncoming traffic and pedestrians facing a red light must stop, so you have the right-of-way to make the left turn. With a solid green or flashing yellow, you may turn left only after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

question: How should you treat a flashing red traffic light?
options: a: Drive through if no traffic.,b: Proceed with right-of-way.,c: Treat it like a stop sign.
note: A flashing red traffic light means you must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe, yielding to any traffic or pedestrians with the right‑of‑way.

question: What does a speed restriction sign indicate?
options: a: It’s blue with black lettering.,b: It can be ignored in bad weather.,c: It shows a recommended speed for curves or turns.
note: A speed restriction sign placed with a curve or turn warning shows a recommended safe speed for that specific condition. It is an advisory speed, not the absolute legal limit, but drivers should treat it seriously and avoid exceeding it, especially in bad weather when traction and visibility are reduced.

question: What is a slow-moving vehicle emblem?
options: a: A circular green sign.,b: A diamond-shaped yellow sign.,c: An orange triangular sign.
note: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle with a red border mounted on the rear of vehicles that usually travel 25 mph or less, such as farm equipment or some construction vehicles. It warns faster traffic to approach and pass with extra caution.

question: When entering traffic from a private driveway, what should you do?
options: a: Yield to vehicles on the main road.,b: Take the right-of-way.,c: Enter only with a traffic light.
note: Traffic already on the main road has the right-of-way. When entering from a driveway or private road, you must wait until there is a safe gap and yield to all vehicles and pedestrians before merging.

question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road?
options: a: Honk to warn others.,b: Stop partially on the roadway.,c: Yield to traffic and pedestrians.
note: Traffic on the main road has the right‑of‑way. When entering from a driveway or private road, you must stop if needed and yield to all vehicles and pedestrians on the roadway and sidewalks, proceeding only when it is safe.

question: A person using a white cane or guide dog is likely:
options: a: Conducting a traffic study.,b: Blind.,c: Deaf.
note: A person using a white cane or a guide dog is legally recognized as blind or visually impaired. Drivers must yield the right-of-way, use extra caution, and never honk or rush them, as they rely on sound and touch to judge traffic.

question: What does a ‘Reduced speed 35 mph’ sign mean?
options: a: New speed limit begins where the next speed limit sign is posted.,b: Maintain your current speed until traffic slows.,c: Begin slowing so you are at 35 mph by the time you enter the reduced speed zone.
note: A “Reduced speed 35 mph” sign is an advance warning that a lower speed limit is ahead. You must begin slowing down so that you are at or below 35 mph by the time you reach the start of the reduced speed zone, which is usually marked by a standard speed limit sign at that point.

question: When turning left, it’s important to:
options: a: Swing to the right side of your lane.,b: Sound your horn.,c: Yield to oncoming vehicles.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians crossing your path. Only start your turn when there is a safe gap. Swinging wide or using your horn does not replace the legal requirement to yield to vehicles and people who have the right‑of‑way.

question: On a two-lane road with opposite traffic, where should you drive?
options: a: In either lane.,b: In the lane with less traffic.,c: In the right lane unless passing.
note: On a standard two-lane road with traffic moving in opposite directions, you must drive in the right lane except when you are legally passing another vehicle or when a lane is blocked. Staying in the right lane helps keep traffic organized and reduces the risk of head‑on collisions.

question: What is the maximum speed you may drive?
options: a: The posted speed limit, regardless of conditions.,b: Any speed faster than other traffic.,c: A speed that is safe and reasonable for current conditions, not exceeding the posted limit.
note: You must always drive at a speed that is safe for current conditions, even if it is lower than the posted speed limit. Factors like traffic, weather, visibility, road surface, and the presence of pedestrians may require you to slow down. The posted speed limit is the maximum allowed under ideal conditions, not a guaranteed safe speed in every situation.

question: Who benefits most from wearing seat belts?
options: a: Drivers only.,b: Passengers on long drives.,c: All vehicle occupants.
note: Seat belts protect everyone in the vehicle by keeping occupants from being thrown around or ejected in a crash. All drivers and passengers, in both front and rear seats, should wear seat belts every trip, regardless of distance.

question: Can you drive around or under a railroad crossing gate being lowered or raised?
options: a: No, you must never drive around or under a moving or lowered gate.,b: Yes, if the train isn’t too close.,c: Yes, if it won’t damage the gate.,d: Yes, if you look carefully.
note: You must never drive around, under, or through a railroad crossing gate while it is being lowered, is down, or is still rising and the warning signals are active. When the lights are flashing or the gate is moving, you must stop and remain stopped until the gates are fully raised and the signals have stopped. It is illegal and extremely dangerous to try to beat a train, regardless of how far away it appears.

question: What does it mean when a driver’s left arm and hand are extended downward?
options: a: Turn left.,b: Turn right.,c: Stop.
note: Hand signals use the left arm: straight out for a left turn, arm up for a right turn, and arm down for slowing or stopping. A left arm extended downward tells other drivers you are slowing or stopping.

question: What does a diamond-shaped sign represent?
options: a: A school crossing sign.,b: An interstate route sign.,c: A road hazard warning sign.
note: Diamond‑shaped signs are warning signs. They alert drivers to road hazards, changes in road conditions, or special situations ahead, such as curves, intersections, or pedestrian crossings. Most are yellow, while orange diamonds are used in work zones.

question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?
options: a: Pass with caution.,b: Do not pass.,c: Slow down.
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means you may not pass vehicles ahead of you in your lane. Yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions, and a solid line on your side indicates that passing from your direction is prohibited because it is unsafe.

question: What do pennant-shaped signs indicate?
options: a: Speed limits.,b: No passing zones.,c: School zones.
note: Pennant-shaped signs (sideways triangles pointing to the right) are used for NO PASSING ZONE warnings. They are placed on the left side of the road to tell you it is unsafe and illegal to start passing other vehicles there.

question: What lane width are motorcycles entitled to?
options: a: Half a lane.,b: The bicycle lane.,c: A full lane.
note: A motorcycle is entitled to use a full traffic lane, just like a car. Other drivers should not crowd a motorcycle or try to share the same lane side‑by‑side, because motorcycles need space to maneuver and maintain a safety cushion.

question: What color are regulatory signs, and must they be obeyed?
options: a: Green, for directions and guidance.,b: Typically white with black or red markings, and mandatory.,c: Blue, for services and information.
note: Regulatory signs tell you what you must do or must not do, such as speed limits, lane use, and parking rules. They are typically white with black or red symbols or lettering, and you are legally required to obey them.

question: What do regulatory signs indicate?
options: a: Present dangers in all locations.,b: What drivers must or must not do.,c: Diamond-shaped warnings.
note: Regulatory signs tell you what you must do or must not do by law, such as speed limits, stop, yield, or no parking. They are usually rectangular with a white background and black or red lettering, and you are legally required to obey them.

question: What separates lanes moving in the same direction?
options: a: Red lines.,b: White lines.,c: Yellow lines.
note: White lines, whether solid or broken, separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions, and red is used for things like reflectors or curbs where stopping or traveling is prohibited.

question: What color are signs in highway work zones?
options: a: School zone signs.,b: Orange.,c: Regulatory signs.
note: Highway work zone warning signs are orange with black symbols or lettering. They alert you to road work and the possible presence of workers, lane shifts, or reduced speeds so you can slow down and drive with extra caution.

question: What does a single dashed white line between traffic lanes mean?
options: a: Passing is allowed if safe.,b: Lanes move in opposite directions.,c: Passing is prohibited.
note: A single dashed white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may change lanes or pass across this line when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: At a light rail intersection, you should always:
options: a: Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.,b: Look both ways before crossing tracks.,c: Obey all traffic signals.
note: At light rail crossings you must always obey all traffic signals and signs, including gates and flashing lights. Looking both ways is important, but your primary legal duty is to follow the signals that control when you may or may not cross the tracks.

question: Why be cautious when large trucks or buses make turns?
options: a: They back up before turning.,b: They yield to all left-turning traffic.,c: They make wide turns and may cross the centerline.
note: Large trucks and buses need more space to turn and often swing wide, sometimes crossing into adjacent lanes or slightly over the centerline. They may also start a turn from a middle lane or appear to move left before turning right. You should never drive into the space they need to turn and should avoid passing them while they are turning, especially on the right.

question: What must you do if a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone?
options: a: Assume the guard shouldn’t be directing traffic.,b: Follow the crossing guard’s instructions.,c: Mimic surrounding traffic despite the guard’s directions.
note: Crossing guards are authorized to control traffic in school zones. You must obey their instructions, slow down, and be prepared to stop for children and pedestrians in or near the crosswalk.

question: What is true about driving on a wet roadway?
options: a: Faster driving reduces tire effectiveness.,b: Water doesn’t affect good tires.,c: Deep water is less dangerous.
note: On wet roads, the faster you drive, the less effective your tires become at gripping the road. Higher speeds increase the risk of hydroplaning, where your tires ride on top of the water and you can lose steering and braking control.

question: When should you slow down while driving?
options: a: At intersections or railroad crossings.,b: On wet or slippery roads.,c: On narrow or winding roads.,d: All of the above.
note: You should slow down in many situations, including at intersections and railroad crossings, on wet or slippery roads, and on narrow or winding roads. Reduced speed gives you more time to react to hazards, stop safely, and maintain control of your vehicle.

question: How should you respond to angry drivers around you?
options: a: Avoid eye contact.,b: Avoid reactive gestures.,c: Distance yourself.,d: All of the above.
note: When dealing with an angry or aggressive driver, your goal is to avoid escalating the situation and create space. Do not make eye contact, do not respond with gestures or yelling, and safely increase your following distance or change lanes to let them go ahead. Using all three strategies together reduces the risk of a road rage incident.

question: What causes many crashes?
options: a: Drivers yielding the right-of-way.,b: Drivers checking mirrors and blind spots.,c: Driving too fast for conditions.
note: Driving too fast for conditions is a major cause of crashes. Even if you are under the posted speed limit, you must slow down when roads are wet, icy, foggy, or when visibility or traffic conditions are poor so you can stop safely.

question: What can help prevent crashes with other road users?
options: a: Communicate with other road users.,b: Ignore other drivers.,c: Drive only on side streets.
note: Crashes are less likely when other road users know what you plan to do. Use turn signals, brake lights, eye contact, and your horn when necessary so drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians can react in time and avoid conflicts.

question: How do you check blind spots when changing lanes?
options: a: Use the inside rearview mirror.,b: Use the outside rearview mirror.,c: Glance over your shoulder.
note: Blind spots are areas you cannot see with your mirrors alone. Before changing lanes, you must quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to be sure no vehicle is in your blind spot.

question: What is the safest way to pass a bicyclist on a two-lane road without bike lanes?
options: a: Slow down and pass with sufficient space.,b: Continue driving, bicyclist moves.,c: Wait for a traffic signal or stop sign.
note: On a two-lane road without bike lanes, you should slow down, wait until it is safe, and then pass the bicyclist while giving them plenty of space—typically at least 3–5 feet where practical. Do not crowd the bicyclist or force them to move; the driver is responsible for making a safe pass.

question: What affects your ability to stop?
options: a: Signal lights.,b: Other cars.,c: Road and weather conditions.
note: Your ability to stop is affected by factors like your speed, road surface, tire condition, brakes, and weather—not by the time of day itself. On wet, icy, or gravel roads, it takes longer to stop, so you must slow down and increase following distance.

question: What should you do before backing out of a driveway with children nearby?
options: a: Rev your engine.,b: Sound your horn.,c: Check behind the car.
note: Before backing, especially where children may be present, you must physically check behind your vehicle. Walk around and look to be sure the area is clear, then back up slowly while continuing to check mirrors and over your shoulder.

question: What is a No zone?
options: a: A no-passing zone.,b: A one-way traffic area.,c: The blind spot of a large vehicle.
note: A No‑Zone is the large blind area around trucks and other big vehicles where the driver cannot see you in their mirrors. If you drive in these areas, the truck driver may not know you are there, increasing the risk of a collision, especially when the truck changes lanes or turns.

question: What steps should you take to change lanes safely?
options: a: Check mirrors and blind spot, then change lanes when safe.,b: Signal, check mirrors, look over your shoulder, then change lanes when safe.,c: Use your turn indicator only; other drivers will adjust.
note: To change lanes safely, you should: signal to let others know your intention, check your rearview and side mirrors, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot, and then move into the lane only when it is clear and safe.

question: When crossing a railroad track with no signals or gates in a line of traffic, what should you do?
options: a: You have the right-of-way.,b: Pass slower drivers.,c: Ensure space to cross fully.
note: When you are in a line of traffic approaching railroad tracks, do not enter the crossing unless there is enough space on the far side for your vehicle to clear the tracks completely. Never stop on the tracks and never pass other vehicles at a crossing.

question: When do roads become very slippery?
options: a: After an hour of rain.,b: The day after rain.,c: In the first 10–15 minutes of a rainstorm.
note: Roads are especially slippery during the first 10–15 minutes of a rainstorm because water mixes with oil and other residues on the road surface. As the rain continues, this mixture is washed away and traction gradually improves, though you should still drive carefully in wet conditions.

question: What should you do when it begins to rain while driving?
options: a: Drive faster than traffic.,b: Drive at the maximum speed limit.,c: Slow down.
note: When rain begins, oil and dirt on the road mix with water and make the surface especially slippery. You should slow down, increase your following distance, and turn on your headlights so others can see you. If heavy rain makes it hard to see, it is safer to pull well off the roadway and wait until conditions improve.

question: Where should pedestrians walk on a road without sidewalks?
options: a: On the side with the lightest traffic.,b: On the side facing oncoming traffic.,c: On the same side as traffic flow.
note: On roads without sidewalks, pedestrians should walk on the side facing oncoming traffic. This lets you see approaching vehicles and react if a driver drifts toward the edge of the road.

question: What headlight setting should you use at night when another vehicle approaches?
options: a: High beam.,b: Low beam.,c: Parking lights.
note: Use low beam headlights when another vehicle is approaching so you do not blind the other driver. High beams should be dimmed when you are within about 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle or when following another vehicle closely.

question: What could cause a crash while driving?
options: a: Taking your attention away from driving.,b: Taking your hands off the wheel.,c: Taking your eyes off the road.,d: Any of the above.
note: Anything that takes your attention away from driving can cause a crash. This includes taking your mind off driving, your eyes off the road, or your hands off the wheel. Mental, visual, and manual distractions all reduce your ability to react to hazards in time.

question: What should you do when driving in bad weather?
options: a: Increase speed to reach your destination.,b: Decrease following distance.,c: Increase following distance.
note: In bad weather, roads can become slippery and it takes longer to stop. You should increase your following distance so you have more space and time to react if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly.

question: What causes highway hypnosis while driving?
options: a: Taking frequent breaks during a trip.,b: Gazing at the road for extended periods.,c: Getting too much sleep before a journey.
note: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead at the road for a long time without actively scanning mirrors, instruments, and the environment. Your mind can drift, and you may not notice slowing or stopped traffic. To prevent this, take regular breaks, shift your focus, and keep your eyes moving.

question: Which commonly causes traffic accidents?
options: a: Inattentive driving.,b: Excessive speed for conditions.,c: Following too closely.
note: Inattentive or distracted driving is one of the most common causes of crashes because drivers may miss traffic signals, stopped vehicles, or changes in road conditions. Excessive speed for conditions and following too closely are also major contributors, but loss of attention to the driving task is a leading factor in many collisions.

question: When should you allow a larger space cushion when stopping?
options: a: At a stop sign.,b: On an incline.,c: At an intersection.
note: On an incline, especially when stopped uphill behind another vehicle, you should leave extra space in front of you. The vehicle ahead may roll backward when starting to move, and the extra space helps you avoid a rear-end collision. Adjusting your space cushion to conditions is an important part of defensive driving.

question: When merging with other traffic, you should:
options: a: Merge regardless of a gap.,b: Wait until your lane ends and merge into a small gap.,c: Allow a gap of about four seconds.
note: When merging, you should adjust your speed to match the flow of traffic and enter when there is a large enough gap. A four‑second gap gives you about a two‑second following distance behind the vehicle in front and leaves room for the vehicle behind you, which helps prevent sudden braking or cut‑offs.

question: What should you do before passing other vehicles?
options: a: Check mirrors and blind spots.,b: Honk three times.,c: Re-enter lane within 10 feet.
note: Before passing, always check your mirrors and blind spots to be sure no one is already in the lane you plan to use. Signal your intention, move into the passing lane when it is safe, and complete the pass promptly. Return to your lane only when you can see the front of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror, leaving a safe following distance.

question: When can you safely pass on a two-way, two-lane street?
options: a: Only when you can see the road ahead clearly.,b: Only when you can see the road ahead clearly, can return to your lane before oncoming traffic, and your vehicle can safely reach the necessary speed.,c: Only when your vehicle can reach the necessary speed.
note: You may pass on a two-way, two-lane road only when all of the following are true: you can clearly see enough clear road ahead, you can complete the pass and return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and your vehicle can accelerate safely to do so. The key legal requirement is that you must be able to return to your lane before you are close to oncoming vehicles.

question: When must you dim your high beam lights?
options: a: When an oncoming vehicle is within 500 feet.,b: When you are following another vehicle within 300 feet.,c: Only on well‑lit city streets.
note: High beams must be dimmed to low beams when an oncoming vehicle is within about 500 feet so you do not blind the other driver. You must also dim your high beams when you are following another vehicle within about 300 feet so your lights do not reflect in their mirrors and reduce their visibility. Always adjust your headlights to avoid impairing other drivers’ vision.

question: What should you do if another driver cuts you off?
options: a: Flash your high beams at them.,b: Pull next to them and yell.,c: Let it go and drive safely.
note: If another driver cuts you off, stay calm, slow slightly if needed, and create space instead of reacting aggressively. Avoid gestures, yelling, or trying to get even, because these behaviors can escalate into road rage and increase the risk of a crash.

question: Which is not a factor in determining vehicle stopping distance?
options: a: Steering ability.,b: Braking distance.,c: Reaction distance.
note: Total stopping distance is the distance your vehicle travels from the moment you see a hazard until you come to a complete stop. It includes perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. Steering ability does not determine how far it takes you to stop; it affects how you can maneuver, not how quickly you can come to a halt.

question: How can you avoid emergency stops in traffic?
options: a: Honk to alert others.,b: Maintain a safe following distance.,c: Drive in the right lane only.
note: You avoid most emergency stops by looking ahead and keeping a safe following distance. This gives you enough time and space to slow down smoothly if traffic stops or a hazard appears, reducing the risk of rear-end collisions.

question: How can you avoid a truck or bus driver’s blind spot?
options: a: Never pass them.,b: Avoid driving alongside or tailgating.,c: Flash your lights at them.
note: Large trucks and buses have big blind spots directly behind them and along both sides, especially on the right. To stay safe, avoid driving right beside or close behind them. Pass promptly and safely, and leave extra following distance so the driver can see you.

question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?
options: a: Honk to alert the bicyclist.,b: Drive in the bicycle lane to pass.,c: Slow down and give ample space.
note: Bicycles are vehicles and need space to maneuver and avoid hazards. When passing, slow down and move over to give them plenty of room, following any state‑specific minimum distance rules, and only pass when it is safe and legal.

question: When should you turn on your headlights?
options: a: Use parking lights only when parked or as allowed by law, not for driving instead of headlights.,b: Drive without any vehicle lights.,c: Turn on your headlights from sunset to sunrise and whenever visibility is reduced, such as at dusk or on overcast days.
note: Headlights must be used from sunset to sunrise and any time visibility is poor, such as at dusk, in rain, fog, or on overcast days. Using your headlights helps other drivers see you as well as improving your own visibility. Parking lights alone are not a substitute for headlights while driving.

question: How can the risk of hydroplaning be reduced?
options: a: Drive through shallow water.,b: Drive more quickly.,c: Drive more slowly.
note: Driving more slowly on wet roads helps prevent hydroplaning because your tires can push water out of the way and maintain contact with the pavement. At higher speeds, a layer of water can build under the tires, causing you to lose steering and braking control.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a: When exiting an expressway.,b: When following a motorcycle.,c: When behind a large vehicle blocking your view.,d: All of the above.
