note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights and siren, you must yield the right-of-way. Safely pull to the right side of the road and stop, or otherwise move to create a clear path so the emergency vehicle can pass quickly and safely.

question: What should you use if your turn signals fail?
options: a: Headlights.,b: Hand signals.,c: Your horn.
note: If your electrical turn signals fail, you must use standard hand and arm signals to indicate turns and lane changes. Extend your left arm straight out for a left turn, bend your left arm up at the elbow for a right turn, and bend your left arm down for slowing or stopping so other drivers can anticipate your actions.

question: If an oncoming vehicle is in your lane, you should:
options: a: Honk to alert the driver, slow down, and steer right if needed to avoid a collision.,b: Speed up and try to pass before they reach you.,c: Maintain your speed and lane position and wait for them to move back.
note: If an oncoming vehicle is in your lane, you should immediately slow down, honk to alert the other driver, and steer to the right to avoid a head‑on collision. Use the shoulder or roadside area if needed. Honking alone is not enough; your main goal is to create space and reduce speed to minimize or avoid impact.

question: What should you do when you hear a fire engine siren behind you?
options: a: Slow down until it passes.,b: Drive with flashers on.,c: Pull over and stop.
note: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, you must pull over to the right side of the road and stop, allowing the emergency vehicle a clear path to pass. Do not just slow down or continue driving with flashers on, because the driver of the emergency vehicle needs a predictable, open lane and space to maneuver quickly and safely.

question: What should you do if you hear a siren but can’t see the emergency vehicle?
options: a: Keep driving until you see it.,b: Pull to the curb and stop.,c: Slow down but don’t stop.
note: When you hear a siren and think an emergency vehicle may be approaching, safely pull over to the right side of the road and stop. Stay stopped until you are sure the vehicle has passed or is not coming toward you.

question: What should you do if your vehicle is blocking traffic after an accident?
options: a: Move it off the roadway if possible.,b: Never move it.,c: Wait for police before moving.
note: If your vehicle is drivable after a minor crash and no one is seriously injured, you should move it out of the traffic lane to the shoulder or a safe area. This helps prevent additional collisions. Turn on your hazard lights, stay at the scene, and exchange information and render aid as required by law.

question: What should you do when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights?
options: a: Slow down and keep moving.,b: Keep driving in your lane.,c: Pull to the right and stop.
note: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaching, you must pull over to the right side of the road and stop until it has passed. Simply slowing down or continuing in your lane can block or delay the emergency vehicle. Stopping on the right creates a clear path in the center or left lanes so the emergency vehicle can get through quickly and safely.

question: What should you do if your vehicle’s right wheels leave the pavement?
options: a: Stop quickly.,b: Pull off the road completely.,c: Slow down and ease back onto the road.
note: If your right wheels drop off the pavement, do not brake hard or jerk the wheel. Ease off the accelerator, keep steering straight and parallel to the roadway, slow down gradually, and when the car is under control and the way is clear, gently steer back onto the pavement.

question: What must you do if an emergency vehicle approaches on a one-way street?
options: a: Speed up to take the nearest exit.,b: Drive with flashers on.,c: Pull over and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using lights or siren, you must yield the right‑of‑way by pulling over to the side and stopping, even on a one‑way street. This gives the emergency vehicle a clear path to pass safely.

question: What should you do if your vehicle’s accelerator sticks open?
options: a: Shift to neutral, brake, and move to the side; then use hazard flashers.,b: Slam on the brakes and turn the ignition off immediately.,c: Keep driving and only turn on four-way flashers.
note: If your accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road, shift to neutral, apply firm brake pressure, and steer to the side of the road. Once you are safely off the roadway and slowing, turn on your hazard flashers to warn others. Do not turn the ignition off while moving, because it can lock the steering or disable power steering and brakes.

question: What should you do when you hear or see an emergency vehicle approaching?
options: a: Stop immediately.,b: Drive to the right and stop.,c: Proceed slowly.
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or siren approaches, you must move to the right side of the road and stop until it has passed. Do not stop in the middle of the lane or in an intersection; instead, pull over safely to the right and wait until the emergency vehicle is well clear.

question: What should you do if someone is injured in an accident you’re involved in?
options: a: Move the injured immediately.,b: Always leave them where they are.,c: Avoid moving them unnecessarily.
note: After a crash, avoid moving an injured person unless there is immediate danger such as fire or risk of another collision. Unnecessary movement can worsen neck, back, or internal injuries. Keep the person warm, reassure them, control severe bleeding with direct pressure, and wait for medical help.

question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with sirens or lights approaches?
options: a: Pull to the right and stop.,b: Pull to the right and slow down.,c: Pull to the right with flashers on.
note: When an emergency vehicle using sirens and/or flashing lights approaches from any direction, you must immediately yield the right‑of‑way by pulling as far to the right side of the road as you safely can and stopping. Remain stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless a police officer directs you otherwise.

question: When must you yield for emergency vehicles?
options: a: Never.,b: When they have flashing lights or sirens.,c: Only if other vehicles yield.
note: You must yield the right‑of‑way to emergency vehicles that are using a siren and/or flashing red, blue, or white lights. Move to the right side of the road and stop, if possible, so they can pass safely. Continue only after the emergency vehicle has passed and it is safe.

question: If followed by a fire engine without emergency signals on a two-lane street, you should:
options: a: Stop quickly.,b: Speed up to clear the way.,c: Continue driving normally.
note: Emergency vehicles only have special right‑of‑way when using their lights or siren. If a fire engine is behind you without emergency signals, obey normal traffic laws and continue driving as usual unless it signals you otherwise.

question: What should you do when approaching an accident scene?
options: a: Focus on driving and keep moving.,b: Stop regardless of involvement.,c: Drive to the scene to look.
note: If you are not involved in a crash and emergency help is already on the way or present, you should keep driving, stay focused on the road, and avoid slowing down just to look. Slowing or stopping to watch an accident can cause additional crashes and block emergency vehicles.

question: If your vehicle skids, how should you steer?
options: a: In the opposite direction of the skid.,b: To keep the front wheels straight.,c: In the direction you want to go.
note: When your vehicle begins to skid, look and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. As the vehicle starts to straighten out, be ready to steer back the other way if needed. Avoid slamming on the brakes, as that can make the skid worse.

question: When an officer is directing traffic at a functioning traffic light, you should:
options: a: Follow the traffic light signals.,b: Honk at the officer.,c: Obey the officer’s directions.
note: When a police officer is directing traffic, their hand signals and instructions override any traffic lights or signs. You must follow the officer’s directions, even if the traffic light shows a different signal.

question: How soon must a vehicle buyer transfer ownership and registration?
options: a: By the deadline required by your state DMV.,b: Within 15 days of purchase.,c: Before the license plate expires.
note: Rules for transferring vehicle ownership and registration are set by each state and the exact time limit varies (commonly around 10–30 days). Because there is no single nationwide 15‑day rule, you must follow your own state’s specific deadline as listed by its DMV.

question: How should you park uphill on a street with a curb?
options: a: Keep front wheel straight.,b: Turn front wheels away from curb.,c: Turn front wheels toward curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb. If the brakes fail, the vehicle will roll back slightly and the front tire will rest against the curb, helping prevent the car from rolling into traffic. For downhill with a curb, you turn the wheels toward the curb; for uphill or downhill with no curb, you turn the wheels so the car would roll away from the roadway.

question: Can you park or stop on the shoulder of a freeway?
options: a: Only in an emergency, such as a breakdown or medical problem.,b: With four-way flashers on.,c: If no part of the vehicle is on the road.,d: To look at a map.
note: Stopping or parking on the shoulder of a freeway is generally prohibited except for emergencies, such as a breakdown, medical emergency, or when directed by law enforcement. Using the shoulder to read a map, make a phone call, or rest is not allowed because it creates a hazard for fast‑moving traffic and for you. If you must stop, exit the freeway and find a safe place off the roadway.

question: Where may you not park?
options: a: On a hill.,b: In a parking lot.,c: On a crosswalk or bike lane.
note: You may not park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane because these areas are reserved for pedestrians and cyclists. Blocking them forces people into traffic and creates a serious safety hazard. Legal parking must also follow local rules, such as staying close to the curb and obeying signs and markings.

question: When parking uphill next to a curb, what should you do?
options: a: Keep rear tires against the curb.,b: Keep front tires straight.,c: Turn steering wheel away from the curb.
note: When parking uphill next to a curb, you should set the parking brake and turn the steering wheel away from the curb. If the vehicle rolls, the front tire will move back and gently touch the curb, stopping the car and preventing it from rolling into traffic. Keeping the wheels straight or toward the curb uphill with a curb does not provide this safety backup.

question: How close to the curb must a vehicle be parked to be legal on a street?
options: a: Within 6 inches.,b: Within 12 inches.,c: Within 18 inches.
note: In many states, you must park with your wheels within about 12 inches of the curb so your vehicle is close enough not to block traffic but not so far that it sticks out into the lane. Always check your state handbook, but 12 inches is a common legal standard.

question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, how should you position your wheels?
options: a: Turn wheels to the right.,b: Turn wheels to the left.,c: Keep wheels straight.
note: When parking downhill on a two-way street, you should turn your front wheels toward the right, toward the curb or roadside. If the vehicle starts to roll, the front tire will move into the curb or off the road edge instead of rolling into traffic. Keeping the wheels straight or turned left could allow the vehicle to roll into the traffic lane.

question: How close can you park to a fire hydrant?
options: a: Within 20 feet.,b: Within 15 feet.,c: Within 10 feet.
note: Parking within 15 feet of a fire hydrant is prohibited.

question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?
options: a: Turn wheels to the left.,b: Turn wheels to the right.,c: Pull up even with the car in front.
note: When parallel parking, after you have checked traffic and signaled, you should first pull up so that your vehicle is parallel and even with the car in front of the space. This starting position gives you enough room to back into the space while turning the wheel at the correct time. Turning the wheels comes after you are properly aligned beside the front vehicle.

question: What should you do if you notice a vehicle defect affecting safety?
options: a: Correct it as soon as possible.,b: Correct it when affordable.,c: Drive slower.
note: Safety‑related defects, such as bad brakes, worn tires, or broken lights, must be fixed before driving. Operating a vehicle with known safety defects greatly increases crash risk and can be illegal, so you should correct them as soon as possible.
